boundary: A local engineering-purpose catalogue derived from the language. These nineteen profiles are not a normative required diagram list. Status describes this reader only, never the scope of SysML. Native candidates are visual reuse candidates, not semantic equivalence claims.

profiles.title: Stakeholders and concerns
profiles.question: Whose question does this view answer?
profiles.typicalForm: Concern–stakeholder–viewpoint–view graph, with an optional coverage register.

profiles.title: System context and boundary
profiles.question: What is inside the system, and what interacts with it?
profiles.typicalForm: System boundary containing parts, external actors or systems outside it, boundary interfaces and declared exchanges.

profiles.title: Use cases and operational objectives
profiles.question: What useful outcome does the system provide to each actor?
profiles.typicalForm: Actor/subject roles with named case nodes, objectives and inclusion links; detailed behavior opens separately.

profiles.title: Interaction scenarios
profiles.question: Who exchanges what, and in which declared order?
profiles.typicalForm: Participants across the top, vertical lifelines and event occurrences, messages between them, nested interactions.

profiles.title: Model membership browser
profiles.question: Where does this element belong in the model?
profiles.typicalForm: Indented expandable model-element list, with ownership/membership icons and references.
requiredSemantics: no occurrence expansion disguised as containment

profiles.title: Definitions, usages and specialization
profiles.question: What is reusable, and how is it used or specialized here?
profiles.typicalForm: Typed definition/usage boxes with compartments and distinct typing, specialization, subsetting and redefinition relationships.

profiles.title: System breakdown and occurrences
profiles.question: What composes this system at this scope?
profiles.typicalForm: Composition tree or nested part boxes; usages show type, multiplicity and contextual occurrence.

profiles.title: Internal structure and interfaces
profiles.question: How do parts connect through their boundary features?
profiles.typicalForm: Nested part boxes with small port/parameter squares on their boundaries, exact connector endpoints and bindings.

profiles.title: Item and information exchanges
profiles.question: What item moves from which source to which target?
profiles.typicalForm: Directed item-transfer graph or detailed flow overlay on a port interconnection view.

profiles.title: Functions and action flow
profiles.question: What actions occur, under which control and data conditions?
profiles.typicalForm: Rounded action nodes, input/output parameters, separate control and item flows, decision diamonds, fork/join bars and performer swimlanes.

profiles.title: Modes and state transitions
profiles.question: Which state changes are allowed, and what causes them?
profiles.typicalForm: Rounded states, nested/parallel regions, entry/do/exit compartments, arrows with trigger [guard] / effect.

profiles.title: Allocation and responsibility
profiles.question: Which target realizes which source intent?
profiles.typicalForm: Two related hierarchies joined by labeled allocation links, or a function-to-component / logical-to-physical matrix.
requiredSemantics: allocation is not connectivity or proof of performance

profiles.title: Requirements and satisfaction
profiles.question: What is required, under which assumptions, and by which subject?
profiles.typicalForm: Requirement boxes with subject, assumed/required constraints and nesting; satisfaction links and a coverage matrix.

profiles.title: Verification planning and evidence
profiles.question: How will each requirement be verified, and what result exists?
profiles.typicalForm: Requirement–verification-case links, a procedure/action view, plus method, configuration and verdict/evidence columns.

profiles.title: Calculations and constraints
profiles.question: Which values are bound, computed or constrained?
profiles.typicalForm: Parameter squares around calculation/constraint nodes, binding lines, equations, quantities and units.

profiles.title: Analysis cases and trade studies
profiles.question: Does the design meet the objective under stated assumptions?
profiles.typicalForm: Analysis case with subject, assumptions, input parameters and calculation workflow; result tables/plots and alternatives.

profiles.title: Geometry and spatial arrangement
profiles.question: Where are the modeled spatial items, and what shapes do they have?
profiles.typicalForm: 2D/3D shapes in coordinate frames, orientation/projection controls, optional quantity color maps.

profiles.title: Variability and configuration
profiles.question: Which alternatives are valid, and which selection is being reviewed?
profiles.typicalForm: Variation/variant tree or feature graph, selection table and validity constraints; overlays on structural views.

profiles.title: Occurrences, time and duration
profiles.question: When do occurrences happen, and what timing is declared or observed?
profiles.typicalForm: Lifelines and ordering for interactions; time-scaled bands or history plots only when actual time/duration facts exist.

demonstration.qualification: Statically qualified source and exact recipe selection; communication-view fidelity tested separately. Bounded support, not complete language or graphical-notation conformance.
